reason: I rank the one-entry panel32 reuse proposals first: the supplied helper already computes each 32-row band, and the proposed outer loop can reduce repeated calls and SME transitions. The two descriptions overlap structurally, so their ranking does not make them distinct experiments; Astra should deduplicate before running a batch. The earlier sixteen-call variant showed mixed paired results and no promotion, so this is only a hypothesis. The coordinated 64 KiB scratch redesign and packed-B panel proposal have plausible reuse goals but change more pointer, layout, and traversal state, raising correctness risk. The two-K control simplifications appear feasible, but the two-step body already exists in the measured history, and prior K-loop schedule variants did not promote; expected benefit is limited and unverified. Transpose fusion and a new transpose-aware primitive carry the greatest implementation or preparation risk. No supplied measurement demonstrates >1800 GFLOP/s or establishes a reuse bottleneck.
